caseStudyHeader.heading: Quarter in Review
caseStudyHeader.body: A digital report for service offering leaders that provides visibility into their offering's readiness, financial performance, and consultant usage.

summary.title: Outcome
summary.description: Within two quarters, the report scaled from 1 offering to 28 offerings and received high engagement with offering teams.

summary.title: Goal
summary.description: The report aimed to provide service offering leaders an adoptable experience that would motivate them to improve the quality of their offering.

summary.title: Role
summary.description: I co-designed this report with another UX designer and my biggest contribution to the project was its user interface and data visualizations.

summary.title: Client and scope
summary.description: The internal client for this project was IBM Services Offering Management and lasted for 6 weeks in early 2020.

context.statement: How might we design a better way for offering leaders to manage their offering's lifecycle?
list: Offering leaders lacked reliable, accessible data to make evidence-based decisions and continually improve their offerings.
The data that did exist was fragmented across platforms and inconsistently formatted, breeding mistrust among offering teams.
Offering leaders often lacked the skills and dedicated time to manage their offering's ongoing performance.
The vision was a quarterly report with the right information, at the right density, to help leaders maintain and evolve high-quality offerings.

subsections.subhead: Offering Content Report user flow: An offering leader receives an email from IBM Services Offering Management inviting them to check out their offering's Quarter in Review report. Upon arriving at the Home view, they can see their Offering's score across three dimensions: usage, health and performance. As they move through each dimension, they are prompted to explore the data in more detail and provided next best actions they can take to improve each dimension. Upon returning back to the Home view, they can share the report with their team.
Design Decision: I used scoring to bring context to data and peer benchmarking to drive behavior change.
Design Decision: The report's executive-level audience drove the data density to be light and data visualizations to be concise and impactful.
Design Decision: I scaled the voice of Offering Management and pushed teams towards lifecycle activities by providing next best steps (A).

outcomes.quote: “I am thrilled to see a report of this nature, every quarter. It not only helps me to assess the progress made, it also helps to focus on area of improvements.”
list: We piloted the report with four offering teams six weeks after design started
76% of users returned within the week and 44% downloaded the full report
Stakeholders approved scaling it from 4 Offerings to 11, then 28 by August 2020
I carried its reporting patterns into Content+, the new content management system
